title: Postmortem: tiered-fallback failed during multi-region queue burst
creator: Lina Morales
summary: A sudden traffic burst into the primary US-EAST pool caused queue growth. The tiered fallback logic routed requests to secondary region (EU-WEST) but a misconfiguration in the circuit-breaker evaluation (queue-depth not included) prevented graceful shedding, causing both regions to breach p99 latency SLOs for ~15 minutes and returning 5xx errors to a subset of Dedicated customers.
impact: ~12% of production requests experienced elevated latency or 5xx errors. Customer-facing SLOs (p99 latency for generation) were missed in US-EAST and briefly in EU-WEST. Two Dedicated customers observed higher error rates and opened support tickets. No data loss or security exposure.
timeline: 2026-03-09T18:12:00Z - Monitoring alert: p99 latency in US-EAST exceeded 4s threshold
2026-03-09T18:13:30Z - Autoscaler started to spin new workers in US-EAST but observed queue depth kept rising
2026-03-09T18:15:00Z - Tiered fallback routing triggered: traffic shifted to EU-WEST model variants
2026-03-09T18:16:20Z - EU-WEST p99 latency begins to climb; circuit-breaker did not open because it evaluated only error ratio, not queue depth
2026-03-09T18:19:00Z - On-call engineer initiated manual throttling of non-critical routes and rolled back a recent batcher tuning change
2026-03-09T18:22:00Z - Traffic normalization observed; p99 latency returned under SLO in both regions
root_cause: Circuit-breaker evaluation logic used only recent error rates and a short sliding window of success/failure counts. It ignored queue depth and request latency percentiles that are early indicators of overload. A recent batcher tuning change increased request coalescing which inadvertently increased queue residence time under bursty traffic, amplifying the overload and delaying breaker tripping. The autoscaler reacted but launch latency meant capacity came too late to avoid SLO misses.
contributing_factors: Batcher tuning change (PR #4576) increased coalescing window which raised instantaneous queue depth during spikes
Circuit-breaker thresholds did not include queue-depth or p95/p99 latency as trip signals
Tiered fallback policy lacks region capacity awareness: it routes by policy but does not check downstream queueing state
Autoscaler warm-up time for GPU-backed workers is non-trivial and is not matched with conservative pre-warming heuristics for known traffic patterns
Runbook lacked explicit guidance to limit fallback during multi-region bursts; on-call actions were manual and slow
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back batcher tuning change within 4 minutes of detection (PR revert and config rollback)
Applied manual route-level throttling for non-essential features to reduce overall token generation load
Adjusted circuit-breaker to an emergency lowered threshold for error rate while we investigated (temporary)
Increased visibility in dashboard: surfaced queue depth and pending-work metrics on main incident board
long_term_actions: CB-1: Extend circuit-breaker evaluation to include queue depth and p95/p99 latency as signals; owner: Arjun Patel; estimate: 5
CB-2: Implement adaptive breaker that uses recent launch-time capacity signals to avoid cascading failovers; owner: Mei Chen; estimate: 8
AS-1: Reduce autoscaler cold-start impact by adding conservative pre-warm policy for peak windows and implement faster provisioning path for critical pools; owner: Rajiv Kumar; estimate: 13
BF-1: Revisit batcher coalescing defaults and add per-tenant safety caps; owner: Lina Morales; estimate: 5

RB-1: Update failover runbook to include queue-depth checks, explicit instructions to avoid broad fallback when secondary shows rising queue depth, and contact list for Dedicated customers; owner: SRE Team; estimate: 3
TEST-1: Add chaos test that simulates large queue bursts in primary region and asserts that tiered fallback preserves SLOs in all regions; owner: Reliability QA; estimate: 8
OBS-1: Create synthetic test that runs p99 latency checks from each region into the tiered fallback path every 5 minutes; owner: Observability; estimate: 3
monitoring_changes: Add queue-depth timeseries to the primary incident dashboard (US-EAST and EU-WEST)
Create a derived alert that fires when queue depth + p95 latency simultaneously exceed thresholds for more than 30s
Add synthetic end-to-end p99 checks for tiered fallback paths with per-tenant visibility
runbook_updates: Document a new decision tree: if primary p99 exceeds SLO and primary queue depth > X, do NOT failover automatically to a single secondary without validating secondary queue depth
Add a checklist for rollback of batcher tuning changes with clear commit and config rollback steps
Include explicit thresholds and runbook steps to escalate Dedicated customer impact to Support and CSM immediately
postmortem_notes: Customer tickets: CS-4491 and CS-4492 opened by Dedicated customers; follow-up scheduled with CSM on 2026-03-13
Postmortem reviewed in reliability-all-hands on 2026-03-11; feedback incorporated into actions

2026-03-11 - Arjun Patel: Confirmed circuit-breaker code path; created CB-1 and CB-2 actions. Added unit tests for error-based breaker behavior.
2026-03-11 - Mei Chen: Noted that fallback policy never checked downstream queue state; will prototype a health-check handshake for routing decisions.
